scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Independent ten-item B2 assessment draft for Somewhere Between Two Cities; human pedagogy approval required.

tabs.title: Applying the Argument
tabs.description: Use the text in new situations.

questions.q: What did Lena's cheerful photographs fail to communicate to Alex?
choices: The names of the places she visited in Rotterdam.
That she could feel isolated despite enjoying the city.
That she regretted accepting the exchange placement.
That her host family had asked her to leave.
questions.explanation: The first paragraph contrasts attractive captions with the loneliness Lena found difficult to admit.

questions.q: Why was the woman's description of bus routes significant to Lena?
choices: It inspired her to take a job as a bus driver.
It convinced her to stop volunteering at the station.
It showed that her own confusion was a shared experience rather than a failure.
It demonstrated that life abroad is mostly about transport.
questions.explanation: The unfamiliar bus routes symbolised the hidden rules newcomers struggle to learn.

questions.q: What does the reaction to the bakery interview suggest about loneliness?
choices: A personal feeling may be widespread even when people hide it.
Radio listeners tend to have more difficulties than other residents.
A good interview can immediately solve social isolation.
Food traditions are the main cause of successful integration.
questions.explanation: The listener responses reveal that seemingly settled people can share the same invisible experience.

questions.q: Why does Lena reconsider sending the old school photograph with a brief joke?
choices: She dislikes the photo now that she has moved abroad.
The picture no longer includes most of her friends.
She thinks Alex will not recognise the building.
She realises it would avoid asking about Alex's real situation.
questions.explanation: The photograph prompts her to question the superficial pattern of messages and reconnect more honestly.

questions.q: Why does Lena say she values the conversations more than the radio certificate?
choices: She has decided to work as a professional journalist.
The conversations have helped her feel connected and rethink her situation.
She will not receive the certificate until she returns home.
The volunteers have promised to pay her for later programmes.
questions.explanation: The unpaid work and shared stories have become a source of belonging and understanding.

questions.q: What makes Lena's invitation considerate rather than demanding?
choices: She promises to cover the full cost of Alex's journey.
She expects Alex to perform for the radio audience.
She offers a visit but also a regular call if travelling is impossible.
She asks Alex to reply before the weekend.
questions.explanation: The final paragraph offers a practical alternative and allows Alex to choose what works.

questions.q: What does Lena acknowledge by saying Alex may have felt left out?
choices: Her curated updates may have damaged their sense of closeness.
Alex has definitely stopped liking their friendship.
Her radio work has prevented Alex from attending college.
She knows exactly what difficulties Alex faces.
questions.explanation: Lena recognises that her apparently effortless life may have made Alex feel excluded.

questions.q: A student posts joyful pictures while finding a new school difficult. Which response best follows Lena's insight?
choices: Delete every photograph taken at school.
Tell all classmates that social media is dishonest.
Avoid discussing the situation with anyone.
Share the difficulty with a trusted friend instead of relying only on captions.
questions.explanation: Lena's central lesson is to allow genuine conversation to replace an edited public image.

questions.q: A newcomer feels embarrassed about not understanding local routines. What advice does Lena's radio experience support?
choices: Find shared experiences through conversations with other newcomers.
Memorise a map before speaking to anyone.
Avoid volunteering until the local language is perfect.
Assume everyone else has always found moving easy.
questions.explanation: Listening to another newcomer's difficulties helps Lena normalise her own experience.

questions.q: Which reply from Alex would best match the kind of friendship Lena wants to rebuild?
choices: A single picture with no accompanying words.
An honest update and a suggestion for a time they could talk.
A list of the best tourist sites in Rotterdam.
An apology for not being able to visit immediately.
questions.explanation: Lena explicitly seeks sincere conversation, not another outwardly cheerful photograph.
